dog.description_text:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.

Pre-Screener Form

Apollo is at risk due to behavior concerns. Despite best efforts, Apollo has not acclimated to his time in care. Apollo is reported to show concerning levels of arousal including heavy panting, barking, inability to settle, and significant leash biting. His leash biting both in and out of kennel make it difficult for him to be handled safely. Apollo has shown concerning levels of dog reactivity. During his assessment, he begins to bark and muzzle punch the door when hearing dogs bark in the neighboring room and will snap at another dog's paw when meeting during a dog greet. According to his previous owner(s), he is social, affectionate, playful, and loves bath time. Medically, Apollo is apparently healthy.

Apollo was first surrendered to the care center as a stray in July 2026 with no known history, and was returned to the shelter by his adopter in October 2026 for behavioral reasons. His previous adopters describe Apollo as an active, playful, social dog who will give you his paw when seeking affection, and loves balls and bath time. At the care center, he has been social and affiliative with staff, though has shown a low threshold for arousal, engaging in kennel fighting and intense leash biting on being removed from his kennel. He is also reported to lunge at dogs, cats, and moving vehicles on leash. Due to these concerns, we recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.
